Playbook.name: Windows — Service Installed with Suspicious Image Path - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A service was installed (4697) with a suspicious image path - cmd.exe, powershell, or an interpreter/encoded command as the service binary. Triage question: is this a persistence/privilege-escalation service, or a legitimate (if unusual) service install?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A service running cmd/powershell/encoded commands is a persistence and SYSTEM-level execution mechanism.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the service was installed.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the suspicious-image-path service is malicious persistence or an unusual-but-legitimate install.

Step.name: Service detail: name, image path, installer
Step.Purpose: The image path content (encoded PowerShell, cmd, temp path) reveals malicious intent.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4697" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.ServiceName, winlog.event_data.ServiceFileName, winlog.event_data.ServiceType | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: ServiceFileName with -enc/-e base64, cmd /c, a temp/appdata path, or an interpreter = malicious. A legitimate app service points at its own signed binary in Program Files.

Step.name: Did the installing account arrive via remote execution
Step.Purpose: A suspicious service installed right after a remote logon/pipe access is attacker persistence via lateral movement.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4624","5145") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType) BY src | SORT c DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A network logon/pipe access from another host just before the install links the persistence to lateral movement - escalate.

Node.Condition: Service image path contains encoded PowerShell/cmd/interpreter or a temp path, especially after remote logon.
An unusual but verifiable legitimate service (vendor app with an interpreter wrapper) under a change record.
Suspicious image path with unclear provenance.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SVCIMG-DETAIL, INV-02-SVCIMG-ORIGIN to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: An unusual but legitimate service install.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the app; close as false_positive.
Stop and remove the service; isolate the host; open IR.
Hunt the installer's origin and other persistence.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A deployment tool creating wrapper services.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
